source_read: PMC HTML, PMC13590218 (Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2010, CD001867.pub3), read in full in my own browser tab: the first 120,000 characters with get_page_text and the remaining 261,000 with javascript_tool. Covered: abstract, plain language summary, background, methods, results (description of studies, risk of bias, effects of interventions), discussion, authors' conclusions, what's new, history, acknowledgements, appendices, the Data and analyses tables for Comparisons 1-6, characteristics of studies, differences between protocol and review, contributions, sources of support and declarations of interest. The forest-plot images were not opened; every number used here is printed in the text or the Data and analyses tables.

claims.overstatement: No overstatement of the Cochrane figures. Two points of scope. (1) The claim's frame ('double-blind trials ... during 12 to 52 weeks of treatment') fits the AHRQ reviews. The Cochrane pool also includes trials as short as 4 weeks (Galarza 1997, Kranzler 1998; 3 months was most common) and four injectable-naltrexone trials, so 'naltrexone in any form, mostly the same tablets' is the right label for its 0.83. (2) The claim gives funding and conflicts only for Jonas 2014. This review was funded by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research, and two of its six authors declare honoraria from drug companies: Leucht from Sanofi-Aventis, BMS, Eli Lilly, Janssen, Lundbeck and Pfizer; Soyka from Lipha, Forest, Sanofi-Aventis, Essex Pharma, Eli Lilly, Prempharm and AstraZeneca. The claim should say so if it lists sponsors for the other reviews.
claims.note: Every Rösner number in the statement and magnitude matches the Data and analyses tables or the text. Return to heavy drinking: RR 0.83 (0.76-0.90), 28 trials, 4433 (Analysis 1.1); NNTB 9.09 (6.66-14.28), given once as 6.67-14.28. Return to any drinking: 0.96 (0.92-1.00), 27 trials, 4693; fixed effect 0.95 (0.92-0.98) (Analysis 1.58); the Discussion once prints 0.92-1.01. Drinking days MD -3.89 (-5.75 to -2.04), 26 trials, 3882. Nausea RD 0.10 (0.07-0.13), 25 trials, 4334. Serious adverse events RD -0.02 (-0.05 to 0.00; the table prints -0.00), 9 trials, 1526. Drop-out because of adverse events RR 1.60 (1.15-2.23), 22 trials, 3393. Naltrexone vs acamprosate (3 trials: COMBINE, Kiefer 2003, Morley 2006; n 800): return to heavy drinking 0.96 (0.87-1.06), any drinking 0.97 (0.91-1.04). Derived from McPheeters' figure arm sizes (Kiefer 40+40, Morley 53+55), COMBINE supplies 612 of these 800 (editors' calculation). Other context: heavy-drinking cut-off 5 (4) drinks for men (women) in most trials; patients were detoxified in most trials, though 7 did not require it and in 3 everyone was drinking at the start; psychosocial treatment in all but 2 trials; mean age 40-50 in 43 of 50 trials, men the majority. Industry-sponsored trials gave RR 0.90 (0.78-1.05) and non-profit trials 0.84 (0.77-0.91); Egger test P = 0.765. Post-treatment (5 trials), heavy drinking RR 0.86 (0.75-0.99). Internal count errors (none affects the claim): funding categories add to 54 (11 industry + 4 unknown + 39 non-profit) and countries to 54 (37 US + 8 Europe + 3 + 3 + 3) for 50 trials; 'nine' men-only trials are named as 11 entries with duplicates; naltrexone vs acamprosate drinking days is 3.06 (-7.42 to 13.53) in the text and 2.98 (-7.45 to 13.42) in the table.

anchors.locator: Methods > Criteria for considering studies for this review (Types of studies, participants, interventions)
anchors.extracted: Double-blind RCTs of opioid antagonists vs placebo or active control in alcohol dependence (people with DSM alcohol abuse no more than 10% of a sample); at least 4 weeks of daily treatment; any dose, mode or combination. Binary outcomes analysed with all randomised patients, drop-outs counted as relapsed.

anchors.locator: Data and analyses, Comparison 1 (NTX versus PBO), outcomes 1-3; Results > Effects of interventions > 01 Naltrexone versus placebo, Treatment phase, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Return to heavy drinking: 28 trials, 4433 participants, RR 0.83 (0.76-0.90), NNTB 9.09 (6.66-14.28). Return to any drinking: 27 trials, 4693, RR 0.96 (0.92-1.00), not significant. Drinking days: 26 trials, 3882, MD -3.89 (-5.75 to -2.04), about 4%.

anchors.locator: Results > Effects of interventions > 01, Sensitivity analyses; Data and analyses, Comparison 1, outcomes 58 and 59
anchors.extracted: Return to any drinking, fixed effect (I² 28%): RR 0.95 (0.92-0.98), significant, so the conclusion depends on the model. By funding: non-profit 0.84 (0.77-0.91), industry 0.90 (0.78-1.05); 26 trials, 4246.

anchors.locator: Results > Effects of interventions > 01, Treatment phase, 3rd paragraph; Data and analyses, Comparison 1, outcomes 7, 22, 39, 46, 52, 54, 55
anchors.extracted: Any side effect RD 0.05 (0.01-0.09), 9 trials; nausea RD 0.10 (0.07-0.13), 25 trials, 4334; vomiting RD 0.07 (0.04-0.09); dizziness RD 0.06 (0.04-0.08); daytime sleepiness RD 0.09 (0.05-0.14). Serious adverse events RD -0.02 (-0.05 to 0.00), 9 trials, 1526. Drop-out because of adverse events RR 1.60 (1.15-2.23), 22 trials, 3393. Any drop-out RR 0.92 (0.83-1.01), 37 trials.

anchors.locator: Results > Description of studies > Included studies (Patients; Treatment setting and study design; Treatment; Outcomes)
anchors.extracted: 50 RCTs (47 naltrexone, 3 nalmefene), 7793 patients; 37 US. Mean age 40-50 in most (43); men the majority. Detoxified in most, with 3-7 to 30 days of abstinence required; 7 trials did not require detoxification, and in 3 everyone was drinking at the start. Oral 50 mg/day in most; higher oral doses in 6; injectable in 4. Treatment 4-52 weeks, 3 months most common; outpatient; psychosocial treatment in all but 2. Heavy drinking was 5 (4) or more drinks for men (women) in most trials.

anchors.locator: Results > Risk of bias in included studies (Allocation; Blinding; Incomplete outcome data; Publication bias)
anchors.extracted: Sequence generation adequately described in 14 of 50; adequate allocation concealment in 3 of 50; adequate blinding in 21. Handling of missing binary data adequate in 11 of 40 and inadequate in 4. Egger test not significant (weighted P = 0.765, n = 29); slight funnel asymmetry.

anchors.locator: Results > Effects of interventions > 03 Naltrexone versus acamprosate; Data and analyses, Comparison 3
anchors.extracted: 3 trials (Anton 2006 COMBINE, Kiefer 2003, Morley 2006), 800 participants: return to heavy drinking RR 0.96 (0.87-1.06), any drinking 0.97 (0.91-1.04). Naltrexone had more nausea (RD 0.08) and acamprosate more diarrhoea (RD -0.27).

anchors.locator: Results > Effects of interventions > 02 Subgroup analyses: Injectable naltrexone; Data and analyses, Comparison 2
anchors.extracted: 4 injectable trials; return to any drinking RR 0.92 (0.84-1.00), 2 trials, 486; drinking days MD -8.54 (-15.77 to -1.31), 2 trials; heavy drinking days -3.05 (-8.46 to 2.35); no pooled return to heavy drinking.

anchors.locator: Discussion > Overall completeness and applicability of evidence; Authors' conclusions > Implications for practice, 2nd paragraph
anchors.extracted: Outcome completeness 56% (heavy drinking), 54% and 52%. Patients were mostly detoxified, on oral 50 mg/day, in outpatient programmes; people with psychiatric comorbidity were screened out. Effects reflect naltrexone added to psychosocial treatment.

anchors.locator: Sources of support; Acknowledgements, last paragraph; Declarations of interest
anchors.extracted: External: German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF grant 01KG0724). Internal: LMU Munich, TU Munich, Chiang Mai University. Leucht and Soyka declare speaker, consultancy or advisory honoraria from several drug companies (Soyka's include Lipha and Forest); the other four authors declare none.

Subgroup rows 59.1 (7 trials, 1121) and 59.2 (19 trials, 3125) checked.
Comparisons 4 and 5: 2 trials, 694 participants, values as stated.
Comparison 6: amount per drinking day 2 trials, 126.

reporting_issues.note: Comparison 6 outcome 4 (2 trials, 694, RD 0.20, 0.14-0.26) duplicates Comparison 4 outcome 4; the nalmefene trials total 396.
The figure legend reads 'outcome: 1.93 Sensitivity analysis: Funding source'; subgroups 7 and 19 trials.
The unweighted SE (1.440) and the funnel-plot wording are identical in Rösner 2010b.
Comparison 5 outcome 6 is RR 1.03 (0.72-1.48) in the table and 1.03 (0.95-1.43) in the text.
Found the 54-trial totals independently. The study tables give Anton 2004 as funded by BioTie Therapies and Martinotti 2008 as Italian, which supports the editors' tally.
Karhuvaara 2007: targeted treatment in the text, heavy-drinker sample in the excluded-studies table.

risk_of_bias.note: AMSTAR 2 low confidence. Item 11 'no' is justified because the item's 'yes' requires investigating the causes of heterogeneity, and the meta-regression was deferred. Single-author study selection (item 5) is confirmed in the Methods.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor is defensible because the abstract reports the null any-drinking result; the 'support abstinence' wording in the implications is the main overreach.

missed: Minor: the Discussion calls heterogeneity high (I² > 75%), but the review's own heterogeneity paragraph gives I² 28% for return to any drinking and only tau² 0.02 (moderate) for return to heavy drinking. The I² > 75% statement applies to drinking days (94%) and heavy drinking days (81%) at most.

For claims citing this review's head-to-head pool: COMBINE contributes about 612 of the 800 participants in Comparison 3 (800 minus Kiefer 80 and Morley 108, using arm sizes shown in McPheeters et al. 2023 Figure 5; editors' calculation), so that comparison rests mainly on one US trial.
